messages.content: 尋找兩家電影院，位於聖地牙哥附近，提供下午5點的《天能》和晚上7點半的《007生死交戰》場次。

function.description: Find local movie theatres and their schedule for a specific movie Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. San Diego, CA

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find two movie theaters near San Diego that have showtimes: 5pm for "Tenet" (天能) and 7:30pm for "007生死交戰" (No Time To Die). We need to use the function find_movie_showing. The function expects location: string, movie: "Tenet" | "No Time To Die"[], time: string[]. So we need to call the function twice? The user wants two theaters. We can call the function twice with different locations? Or we can call once with location "San Diego, CA" and movie array containing both movies? But the function signature: movie: "Tenet" | "No Time To Die"[] means movie can be either "Tenet" or "No Time To Die" or an array of those? Actually the type says movie: "Tenet" | "No Time To Die"[], which is ambiguous. It might mean movie can be either "Tenet" or an array of "No Time To Die"? That seems wrong. Probably they intended movie: ("Tenet" | "No Time To Die")[] meaning an array of either movie. So we can pass movie: ["Tenet", "No Time To Die"].

Time: string[]: we need times for each movie. We could pass times: ["5:00 PM", "7:30 PM"].

But the function likely returns theaters that match both movies at those times. But the user wants two theaters: one with 5pm Tenet, another with 7:30pm No Time To Die. So maybe we need to call twice: first for Tenet at 5pm, second for No Time To Die at 7:30pm. But the user wants two theaters. So we can call twice with same location "San Diego, CA" but different movie/time combos. That will return theaters that match each query. Then we can combine results.

Thus we should call find_movie_showing twice: first with movie "Tenet" and time ["5:00 PM"], second with movie "No Time To Die" and time ["7:30 PM"]. Provide location "San Diego, CA".

Let's do that.
